claim: When flushing is driven by redo age and the adaptive flushing cap (innodb_io_capacity_max) is below what it asks for, the redo log fills and commits stall on sync flushes: raising the cap raises throughput.
note: 2026-11-04 first design failed: io_capacity 200 / 2000 / 10000 on 8 x 16M with a 4 GB pool - flushing was LRU-driven (data far larger than the pool) and io_capacity_max stays >= 2000 by default, so the cap never bound (flushing asked for 0.25% of it). Now in memory (~8 GB in 12 GB), a 1 GB redo log so flushing follows redo age (redo/positive: 100% by age at 512 MB), and the cap that binds adaptive flushing swept with io_capacity fixed at 200.
